diagnosis: Writes the full sum of the ones place beside the sum of the tens place instead of regrouping ten ones into a ten.
rationale: The student computed 7 + 6 = 13 and 3 + 2 = 5, writing them side-by-side as 513. The place-value / make-a-ten tool directly addresses this by demonstrating how a group of ones greater than 9 bundles into one ten and leftover ones.

script.focus: ten ones bundling into one ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [15]. Tutor points at: ten ones bundling into one ten

frames.caption: Here are 15 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 5 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place: 15. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they wrote 13 in the ones place rather than regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. This detour uses a clean place-value chart demonstration with 15 ones, explicitly addressing the rule that a place can only hold digits 0-9 and showing the bundle of ten ones moving to the tens place. It addresses the exact misconception using an analogous number (15 instead of 13) without leaking the exact answer.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this demo directly targets the misconception that more than 9 ones can stay in the ones place by clearly demonstrating bundling ten ones into one ten.
